misconception_description: Student believes that in the expression x == a or b, the comparison operator distributes to both operands of the or operator.

solutions.generated_code:
program JumlahHarmonik
kamus
  n, i : integer
  jumlah : real
algoritma
  input(n)
  if n == 1 or 2 then
    output(1)
  else
    jumlah <- 0
    for i <- 1 to n do
      jumlah <- jumlah + 1 / i
    endfor
    output(jumlah)
  endif
endprogram

metadata.modification_notes: The student modified the base case condition from `if n == 1:` to `if n == 1 or 2:`, believing this checks whether n equals 1 or n equals 2. However, this expression evaluates to `(n == 1) or 2`, which is always True because 2 is a truthy value. This means the function will always return 1 immediately for any input, never performing the recursive calculation. The student genuinely believes they're adding an additional base case to handle n==2, thinking the comparison operator distributes across the or operator.
